args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
WHITLOCK & CROSS LLP — INTERNATIONAL TRADE & SANCTIONS GROUP

MEMORANDUM

TO:      Deal Team — CFIUS National Security Agreement
FROM:    Associate, International Trade & Sanctions Group
RE:      Counterparty Markup Analysis — CFIUS National Security Agreement ("NSA",
         draft dated as circulated) — Risk-Prioritized Markup Memo with
         Recommendations and Counter-Draft Language
DATE:    [Current Date]
ENGAGEMENT: Review the counterparty markup against the draft NSA and supporting
         materials; produce a risk-prioritized memo with recommendations and
         counter-draft language for each material change. Output: markup-analysis-memo.docx

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I.   SCOPE AND DOCUMENT SET CONSIDERED
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This memorandum reconciles the counterparty's revised National Security Agreement
("markup") against the draft NSA, the disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the deal
team's controlling negotiation instructions. In preparing this memo I reviewed in
full the materials filed in this matter's folder:

   •   Deal materials — CFIUS National Security Agreement (input/operative record);
   •   Counterparty markup of the NSA (the revision under review);
   •   Schedules and exhibits to the NSA (disclosure schedules and survival matrix);
   •   Deal team correspondence (partner email thread, including the controlling
       revised priority instruction);
   •   Administrative correspondence (misfiled, unrelated engagement — NOT relied on
       and excluded from this analysis).

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces
three material deviations that must be reconciled against the base materials. Each
is analyzed below in descending order of risk, with a recommendation, the relevant
conflict in the base materials, and counter-draft language.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
II.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF RISK-ORDERED DEVIATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

RISK 1 (HIGH — WALK-AWAY):  Elimination/reduction of the survival period for the
      core representations (limitation-period change). The counterparty shortens the
      survival of core reps. This contradicts Exhibit B (survival matrix), and deal
      team instruction treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue.
      RECOMMENDATION: REJECT — do not concede any reduction.

RISK 2 (HIGH — PROTECT):  MAE/Material-Adverse-Effect definition expanded with new
      carve-outs for "regulatory action of the kind at issue." Schedule 3.7 discloses
      two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs, which would
      enable the counterparty to walk or avoid indemnity using the very regulatory
      matters at issue in this matter.
      RECOMMENDATION: REJECT / NARROW — delete the new carve-outs or make them
      subject to the existing regulatory-inquiry exceptions and a reasonableness
      standard.

RISK 3 (MEDIUM — CONCEDE ONE ELEMENT):  Indemnification cap silently reduced and
      basket converted from a deductible to a tipping basket. Per the controlling
      instruction, the client WILL CONCEDE the basket (deductible→tipping) conversion.
      However, the silent cap reduction is NOT conceded and would, combined with
      Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), silently shift retained liabilities to the
      client.
      RECOMMENDATION: ACCEPT the basket conversion as directed; REJECT the cap
      reduction; counter-draft to preserve the cap and the Schedule 5.2 allocation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DETAILED ANALYSIS, RECOMMENDATIONS, AND COUNTER-DRAFT LANGUAGE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

RISK 1 — SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS
      (WALK-AWAY ISSUE; REJECT)

   What the markup does. The counterparty adds a new limitation period that shortens
   the survival of the core representations (reps & warranties). A survival-period
   reduction compresses the time within which the client may bring a claim for
   breach, directly reducing remediation exposure on the most important reps.

   Conflict with base materials. Exhibit B to the NSA sets the survival matrix and
   the base materials' firm-standard survival periods for the core reps. The markup's
   limitation-period change directly contradicts Exhibit B. Per the governing rule,
   the scheduled exceptions (Exhibit B) control over general statements and the
   markup's change cannot override the survival matrix.

   Deal team guidance. The latest controlling message is unambiguous: the client
   treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier correspondence
   that suggested flexibility on survival is superseded and does not control.
   Accordingly, there is no permissible concession band on this term.

   Recommendation. REJECT the change as a walk-away issue. Make no concession. If the
   counterparty presses, return to the Exhibit B survival matrix verbatim.

   Counter-draft language:

      "Survival. The representations and warranties of the Seller shall survive the
      Closing until the expiration of the applicable survival period set forth in
      Exhibit B (the 'Survival Period'). No provision of this Agreement shall be
      construed to shorten, suspend, or eliminate the Survival Period for any
      representation or warranty set forth in Exhibit B, and any attempted
      modification or reduction of such Survival Period shall be void and of no
      force or effect."

   (Delete from the markup the counterparty's new limitation period in its entirety.)

   Risk posture if accepted: High. Acceptance would materially shorten the client's
   ability to assert claims on the core reps and would constitute a walk-away per
   client instruction.

RISK 2 — MAE DEFINITION CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
      (HIGH RISK; REJECT/NARROW)

   What the markup does. The counterparty adds carve-outs to the definition of
   "Material Adverse Effect" ("MAE") for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at
   issue in this matter." As drafted, these carve-outs would except from an MAE (and
   from the corresponding remedies) any adverse effect caused by CFIUS/regulatory
   action of the type giving rise to this engagement.

   Conflict with base materials. Schedule 3.7 to the NSA discloses two pending
   regulatory inquiries. Those inquiries intersect precisely with the new MAE
   carve-outs. As marked up, the counterparty could rely on its own or third-party
   regulatory action — including the very inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 — to
   defeat a client MAE claim or to avoid an indemnity obligation. The schedules
   qualify the operative materials and, because the carve-outs were introduced solely
   to capture regulatory events of the kind disclosed, they cannot be reconciled with
   the scheduled exceptions.

   Deal team guidance. The controlling instruction preserves the client's ability to
   treat regulatory-adverse effects consistently with Schedule 3.7. No instruction
   authorizes conceding these carve-outs. The risk here is compounded because the
   carve-outs track the exact regulatory events disclosed in the schedule.

   Recommendation. REJECT the new carve-outs. At minimum, narrow them so that they
   (i) do not apply to regulatory action arising from or relating to the matters
   disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and (ii) are qualified by a reasonableness/causation
   standard. Because Schedule 3.7 lies at the center of this matter, recommend
   outright deletion.

   Counter-draft language:

      "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the definition of 'Material
      Adverse Effect' in this Agreement, no effect shall be excluded from an MAE
      if such effect arises out of, relates to, or results from any pending,
      threatened, or prospective action, inquiry, investigation, or proceeding by
      any Governmental Entity (including any CFIUS-related action) that relates to
      the matters described in Schedule 3.7, regardless of whether such action is
      disclosed, commenced, or threatened before or after the date hereof. Any
      purported carve-out for regulatory action shall be subject to this Section and
      shall require that the counterparty not have caused or contributed to the
      relevant regulatory action."

   Risk posture: High. Acceptance would permit the counterparty to nullify MAE-based
   remedies by invoking the very regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.

RISK 3 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCED AND BASKET CONVERTED TO TIPPING
      (CONCEDE BASKET CONVERSION; REJECT CAP REDUCTION)

   What the markup does. The counterparty (i) silently reduces the indemnification
   cap and (ii) converts the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket
   (i.e., once the basket threshold is exceeded, the entire amount, including amounts
   below the threshold, becomes recoverable, rather than only the excess).

   Conflict with base materials. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. The markup's
   indemnification changes would silently shift a portion of those retained
   liabilities back onto the client. The base materials allocate those liabilities to
   the counterparty; the markup's cap reduction undermines that allocation.

   Deal team guidance. The controlling instruction is explicit: the client WILL
   CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping). The client does NOT concede
   the cap reduction. Therefore, the basket conversion is the only permissible
   concession on this deviation.

   Recommendation. (i) ACCEPT the basket conversion, as directed, but confirm the
   dollar threshold and application remain otherwise unchanged. (ii) REJECT the cap
   reduction and counter with the firm-standard cap; confirm that Schedule 5.2
   retained liabilities continue to sit with the counterparty and are not shifted by
   the cap change.

   Counter-draft language:

      "Indemnification Cap and Basket. The aggregate liability of the Seller for
      indemnification claims under Article [__] shall not exceed the 'Cap' (as
      defined in Section [__]), and no change in the Cap set forth in the base draft
      shall be effective. For purposes of this Article, indemnification claims shall
      be recoverable only to the extent that the aggregate amount of Losses exceeds
      the 'Basket' (as defined in Section [__]) (a 'deductible' basket); provided,
      however, that for the limited purpose of the [operational-loss] claims set
      forth in Section [__] and per the parties' agreement, once aggregate Losses
      exceed the Basket, the full amount of such Losses (including amounts below the
      Basket) shall be recoverable (a 'tipping' basket). Nothing in this Section
      modifies the allocation of the retained liabilities set forth on Schedule 5.2,
      which shall remain solely the responsibility of the Seller."

   Risk posture: Medium. The basket conversion is conceded and creates no incremental
   exposure beyond what client endorsed. The cap reduction, if accepted, would
   silently shift Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; it must be rejected.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV.  ADDITIONAL RECONCILIATION NOTES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

   •   Schedules control. Per the governing rule, the disclosure schedules
       (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2) and Exhibit B (survival matrix) control over any
       general statement in the base materials and in the markup. Every counter-draft
       above preserves those scheduled exceptions.

   •   Distractor excluded. The administrative correspondence misfiled into the folder
       concerns an unrelated engagement. It has been excluded from this analysis and
       must not be cited or relied upon for this matter.

   •   Superseded guidance. Any earlier deal-team message stating the opposite
       priority ordering (e.g., flexibility on survival, insistence on the basket) is
       superseded by the latest controlling instruction and is disregarded.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
V.   CLOSING RECOMMENDATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

   1. Survival period — REJECT (walk-away). Do not concede any reduction; return to
      the Exhibit B survival matrix.
   2. MAE carve-outs — REJECT/NARROW. Delete the regulatory-action carve-outs, at
      least as they would apply to the Schedule 3.7 inquiries.
   3. Indemnification cap — REJECT the cap reduction; ACCEPT the basket conversion
      per client instruction; preserve the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability
      allocation.

This memorandum reflects the risk-prioritized analysis of the counterparty markup
against the draft NSA and supporting materials. Counsel should circulate the
counter-draft language to the counterparty without yielding on the walk-away
survival term, and should treat the MAE carve-outs as effectively non-negotiable
given their direct intersection with the disclosed regulatory inquiries.

[end of memorandum]
